messages:
Anna Park: Quick sync — need a decision on the stability policy for legacy routes and the deprecation timeline. Customers are asking for clarity. Proposing a schedule and migration support plan by EOW.
Mike Chen: +1 on schedule. Can we aim for a 9-month window: 6 months migration + 3 months critical/security-only support? Keeps ops burden reasonable.
Sara Patel: FYI we currently have 4 enterprise accounts still on the old routes; at least 2 will need hands-on migration help. They also use tool-calling heavily.
Devon O'Neill: Technical constraints: function-calling payloads changed shape in vNext and structured output has a stricter schema. We should provide a translation shim and contract tests.
Luca Rossi: From product perspective we need clear launch criteria before marking vNext as the default: (1) parity on major endpoints (chat, embeddings, rerank), (2) migration tooling available, (3) no >1% client errors in canary.
Anna Park: Agree. Also need to define what constitutes a breaking change vs. additive change. My proposal: additive enhancements = no deprecation; contract/shape changes = breaking -> require migration window.
Mike Chen: Implementation notes: we can do a server-side compatibility layer that maps v1 params to vNext for common cases. It won't cover every edgecase (especially custom function schemas). Suggest shipping the shim as a feature flag for Dedicated/Private too.
Sara Patel: For customers, provide three paths: (A) auto-shim (best-effort), (B) SDK compatibility helpers with codemods, (C) 1:1 migration support for enterprise commits. Pricing for (C) is ok.
Devon O'Neill: We'll also need automated regressions—run prompts against both routes to surface quality deltas. I can add a nightly job that computes token-level and semantic-fluency diffs.
Luca Rossi: Can we define metrics to gate deprecation? Propose: <0.5% API errors across representative traffic, latency within 10% of v1 for p95, and semantic-similarity >= 0.95 on eval prompt set.
Anna Park: Nice. Next: docs & timeline. Draft timeline: Week 0: announce deprecation intent + migration guide draft. Week 4: release SDK helpers and codemods. Week 12: enable opt-in shim for all hosted customers. Month 6: opt-out period ends; set default to vNext for new keys. Month 9: v1 sunset (security-only).
Mike Chen: Feels reasonable. We should also publish a migration checklist with examples for chat->completions mapping and function-calling deltas. Example snippet for shim:
```
# shim map (pseudo)
if route == '/v1/chat' and body.contains('functions'):
  body.rename('messages','input')
  body.wrap('functions', 'tools')
```
This is best-effort; call out unsupported cases in logs.
Sara Patel: Can CS prepare a customer comms draft highlighting opt-in shim and migration offers? We should tag customers by usage: embeddings-heavy vs chat-heavy vs tools-heavy.
Devon O'Neill: Also engineering needs a compatibility test harness. Proposal: add an "api-compat" pipeline that runs nightly comparing outputs for a curated prompt set across models and quantization profiles.
Luca Rossi: Launch criteria checklist to own: docs, SDKs, shim, canary metrics, CS playbook, and migration web-runbooks. When all green, flip default for new keys.
Anna Park: Action items: Mike -> prototype shim + performance numbers by next sprint. Devon -> compat harness + eval metrics. Sara -> CS comms + customer list. Luca -> finalize launch checklist and legal sign-off. I'll draft the public timeline.
Mike Chen: I'll also add opt-in header: `X-Use-Legacy-Shim: true` so customers can control.
ProductBot: Reminder: create incident channel #prod-v1-deprecations once timeline is public.
Sara Patel: Thanks — I'll schedule customer town hall for Week 1 after announcement.
Anna Park: Great. If no objections, I'll post the deprecation intent announcement tomorrow morning and attach the draft migration checklist. :thumbsup:
Luca Rossi: No objections from me.
Devon O'Neill: Fine by eng.
Mike Chen: Fine from infra.
Sara Patel: Fine from CS.
Anna Park: Closing this thread — will share the announcement draft in #product-drafts for review.
